title: Primitive fixed-vector polynomials imply arbitrary symmetric-power lifts over a DVR
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $H$ be a flat affine finitely presented group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with the group-object diagrams interpreted over this base. A rational $H$-module is an $A$-module $M$ with $A$-linear coaction $M\to M\otimes_A A[H]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities, where $A[H]=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_H)$ has the coordinate Hopf algebra maps; fixed vectors satisfy $\rho(m)=m\otimes1$. Equivariance means commutation with coactions. Tensor and dual modules have diagonal and contragredient coactions. Write $\operatorname{Sym}^n_A M$ for the degree-$n$ part of the commutative algebra freely generated by $M$, with the induced coaction. Suppose that for every finite free rational $H$-module $V$ and every primitive invariant vector $v\in V^H$ (that is, $v\notin\mathfrak mV$), there exist $n\geq1$ and $f\in(\operatorname{Sym}^n_A(V^\vee))^H$ with $f(v)=1$, where $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(V,A)$ and evaluation sends a product of linear forms to the product of their values. Then For every rational $H$-module $M$, with no finiteness or flatness assumption, and every equivariant surjective $A$-linear map $\lambda:M\twoheadrightarrow A$ to the trivial module, there exist $n\geq1$ and $q\in(\operatorname{Sym}^n_A M)^H$ such that $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\lambda)(q)=1$, under $\operatorname{Sym}^n_A A\simeq A$.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5(5),(5-double-prime), Remark 9.2.4(i), and Lemma 4.1.8, printed pp.502--504,521--523. Corrected primitive-vector form of Remark 9.2.7: dualize a surjection from a finite free module, rather than an arbitrary injection A into V. The resolution property over a DVR and Noetherian approximation remove all restrictions on M. Local PDF WANTED; read https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf

proof.text: Put $B=A[H]$. The DVR is Noetherian since all its ideals are principal. Its affine spectrum $U$ is Noetherian, and $H$ is Noetherian by finite presentation (hence finite type) and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The groupoid $H\rightrightarrows U$ has both structure maps flat and affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus the Noetherian and flat hypotheses of [lem-sfb-flat-noetherian-groupoid-coherent-approximation] hold. This argument needs no regularity of completion and no reductivity.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5 (5),(5-double-prime), Remarks 9.2.4(i),9.2.7, pp.521--523; explicit dual-surjection argument; finite approximation via Stacks groupoids.tex Tag 07TU, lemma-colimit-coherent.

proof.text: Use the quasi-coherent sheaf $\widetilde M$ on $U$ of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Its equivariance isomorphism on $H$ is, on affine sections, $m\otimes b\mapsto\sum m_{(0)}\otimes m_{(1)}b$ when $\rho(m)=\sum m_{(0)}\otimes m_{(1)}$; the inverse replaces $m_{(1)}$ by its antipode. The inverse identities are the Hopf antipode identities, and the cocycle and unit identities are precisely coassociativity and the counit identity. Conversely an equivariance isomorphism evaluated at $m\otimes1$ recovers the coaction; its module-map condition is exactly the coaction condition for morphisms. These statements are checked using the affine pullback formula in [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections]. Thus coherent groupoid modules in an approximation give finite rational modules on taking affine sections.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5 (5),(5-double-prime), Remarks 9.2.4(i),9.2.7, pp.521--523; explicit dual-surjection argument; finite approximation via Stacks groupoids.tex Tag 07TU, lemma-colimit-coherent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-noetherian-groupoid-coherent-approximation] to $\widetilde M$ and [lem-sfb-groupoid-module-limits-colimits] to forget equivariance: the underlying quasi-coherent module is the colimit of coherent modules $F_j$. On an affine scheme, the associated-sheaf/section correspondence follows from [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change]: on each principal open both sides are the localization of global sections, so the canonical maps and their inverses glue. Consequently it preserves colimits. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], any chosen $m\in M$ with $\lambda(m)=1$ is the image of some $x\in\Gamma(U,F_j)$. Set $N=\Gamma(U,F_j)$ and let $u:N\to M$ be the cocone map. It is equivariant by the preceding coaction formula and is finite over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-affine-sections-finite]. The composite $\lambda u$ is surjective since it sends $x$ to $1$. Neither $u$ nor the transition maps need be injective.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5 (5),(5-double-prime), Remarks 9.2.4(i),9.2.7, pp.521--523; explicit dual-surjection argument; finite approximation via Stacks groupoids.tex Tag 07TU, lemma-colimit-coherent.

proof.text: Take an equivariant finite free cover $p:P\twoheadrightarrow N$ from [lem-sfb-dvr-rational-module-finite-free-cover]. Write $a=\lambda up:P\twoheadrightarrow A$. In $V=P^\vee$ the vector $v=a$ is invariant: after every scalar extension, $(h\cdot a)(z)=a(h^{-1}z)=a(z)$ since $a$ is equivariant to the trivial module. It is primitive: choose $z\in P$ with $a(z)=1$; if $a\in\mathfrak mP^\vee$ then every value of $a$, including $a(z)$, belongs to $\mathfrak m$, a contradiction. Apply the assumed primitive-fixed-vector polynomial property to this finite free $V$ and $v$, obtaining $n\ge1$ and invariant $f\in\operatorname{Sym}^n(V^\vee)$ with $f(v)=1$.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5 (5),(5-double-prime), Remarks 9.2.4(i),9.2.7, pp.521--523; explicit dual-surjection argument; finite approximation via Stacks groupoids.tex Tag 07TU, lemma-colimit-coherent.

proof.text: The finite free bidual map $b:P\to(P^\vee)^\vee$, $b(z)(\ell)=\ell(z)$, is an equivariant isomorphism: a basis and its dual give the inverse, and $(h\cdot b(z))(\ell)=b(z)(h^{-1}\ell)=\ell(hz)=b(hz)(\ell)$. Let $q$ be the image of $f$ under $\operatorname{Sym}^n(upb^{-1})$. The symmetric map exists by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property], preserves degree by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded], and is equivariant by applying the coaction identity to each factor of a product. Hence $q$ is invariant. On a product $b(z_1)\cdots b(z_n)$, evaluation at $v=a$ is $\prod_i a(z_i)$, which is also its image under $\operatorname{Sym}^n(a b^{-1})$. Products span degree $n$, so the two linear maps agree on $f$. Therefore $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\lambda)(q)=f(v)=1$.
